To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the chronic ethanol treatment and its subsequent withdrawal produce significant decreases in GR protein expression and GRE-DNA-binding in various brain structures, and these changes are significantly attenuated by chronic mianserin treatment.
the chronic ethanol treatment decreased glucocorticoid (GRs) protein expression in the cortex, hippocampus, and amygdaloids and decreased GRE-DNA-binding in the cortex and hippocampus.

chronic ethanol administration and withdrawal decreased the expression of glucorticoid receptors and glucorticoid response element -DNA binding in the brain of rat, which may be responsible for altered hypothalamic pitutary adrenal axis function during ethanol withdrawal.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms of ethanol-induced changes in HPA axis, which may be involved in alcohol dependence.
elucidating the molecular mechanisms of alcoholism.
the role of 5-HT and GR in alcohol dependence.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the decreased GR expression in the PVN and hippocampus may be responsible for abnormal HPA axis activity during ethanol exposure and ethanol withdrawal.
chronic ethanol treatment and ethanol withdrawal significantly decreased the expression of GR and GRE-DNA-binding proteins in various brain structures, but the effects were not uniform.

the GR expression and GRE-DNA interaction in various brain structures are altered during ethanol exposure and its withdrawal, and these alterations are modulated by mianserin, a 5-HT(1A/2A/2B) antagonist, which is a potential therapeutic drug for the treatment of alcohol dependence.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

ethanol withdrawal produces a down-regulation of GRs in the rat brain, especially in the PVN, and that the down-regulation of hippocampal GRs may be involved in the development of ethanol withdrawal-induced behavioral changes.

ethanol treatment and its subsequent withdrawal produced differential alterations in GRs and GRE-DNA-binding proteins in various brain structures, and these changes were significantly modulated by 5-HT(1A/2A/2B/2C) receptor antagonist mianserin.

the 5-HT(1A) receptors may be involved in the modulation of GR protein expression in hippocampus, but 5-HT(3) receptors are involved in the regulation of GR protein expression and GRE-DNA interaction in the cortex.
The main takeaway from our work is that
5-HT( 2 A/2C) receptor antagonism may have therapeutic potential for treatment of ethanol dependence.
chronic ethanol administration and its withdrawal significantly decreased GR expression in various brain structures.
alcohol exposure and withdrawal modulate GR expression in a region-specific manner, and the interaction of GRs with serotonin (5-HT) receptors may play a role.
